## Command Details

```text
Grant, revoke, consume, and inspect Approvals — the human
authorizations a Decision settles under (F050): scoped, expiring,
revocable, and single-use. One authorization can never be replayed.

The registry is governed state, not incidental metadata: an
append-only event ledger under .amber/approvals/ (granted, revoked,
and consumed events; no in-place mutation path) protected by a
tamper-evident hash chain (a fold over an edited ledger fails closed
as corruption), serialized by a short-lived write lock (a second
writer in flight fails closed as AMBER_E_APPROVAL_REGISTRY_LOCK; a
lock older than 30 s is reclaimed as stale), fail-closed on
corruption and on schema versions this reader does not support, with
a size ceiling (AMBER_APPROVAL_MAX_REGISTRY_BYTES; default 1 MiB; an
append that would exceed it is refused before any durable state is
touched).

An Approval is a human-only authorization slot: the approver (and the
revoker) are verified against the Principal registry — registered,
unrevoked, inside their validity window — and must be human; the
verified snapshot is frozen into the event. The validity window is
half-open [validAt, validUntil) under a recorded clock source and the
no-tolerance skew policy: at exactly validUntil the authorization is
already expired. validAt (when the window opens) and recordedAt (when
the record was written) are stored as distinct fields.

Consumption is atomic with the authorized Decision's settlement: the
consume writer admits one Decision artifact (decisionKind approval,
principal = the approval's frozen approver) and appends the consumed
event binding that Decision's identity and revision — if the
admission fails, no consumed event is written and the authorization
stays unconsumed. A second consumer (racing or serial) fails closed
as AMBER_E_APPROVAL_ALREADY_CONSUMED; consumption is terminal, so a
consumed approval can no longer be revoked. When the approval carries
a scope, the Decision is admitted with that same scope. Derived status
(granted | revoked | consumed | expired) is computed at read time,
never stored.

Subcommands:
  grant --id <id> --approver <human-principal> --subject <what>
        Grant one authorization. --valid-until <iso> is the required
        expiry instant (ISO-8601; a date-time must carry an explicit
        zone); --scope <tag> is an optional confinement tag.
  revoke --id <id> --revoker <human-principal>
        Revoke terminally (revocation is a human act; history is
        never rewritten).
  consume --id <id> --decision-identity <identity> --body <markdown>
        Settle the authorization as one approval Decision.
        --trace decides:<type>:<identity> names the artifact revision
        the Decision decides (the Decision admission's required
        lineage); --scope must match the approval's scope when it
        carries one.
  show --id <id>        Show one derived record (status, decision
        binding when consumed).
  list                  List every derived record in grant order.
Confirmation proof (issue #340): grant and consume require a human
confirmation before any ledger write. In an interactive terminal
answer the y/N prompt; everywhere else pass --yes to record a flag
confirmation. Without either, the writer is refused loudly as
AMBER_E_APPROVAL_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and nothing is written. The
collected proof is recorded on the ledger event as
confirmation.method ("flag (--yes)" or "user (interactive)").

Examples:
  amber approval grant --target . --id approval/login-42 --approver alice@example.com --subject spec/login@2 --valid-until 2027-01-31 --scope team-a --yes --json
  amber approval consume --target . --id approval/login-42 --decision-identity decision/login-approved --body 'Approved after review.' --trace decides:spec:spec/login --yes --json
  amber approval revoke --target . --id approval/login-42 --revoker alice@example.com --json
  amber approval show --target . --id approval/login-42 --json
  amber approval list --target . --json
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines these target-relative paths, refusing `..` and symlink escapes before reading or writing: plan and scaffold destinations (including `accept --plan`), memory and context payloads, harness inputs, adapter allow-lists, workflow reports and their output directory, ledger exports, execution readiness plans, session and worktree state, governance report output, wiki export and handoff bundle output directories.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing, and the confinement above covers only the surfaces it names, and a confined flag still accepts an absolute destination only when it stays inside the target. `governance audit --output`, `governance readiness --output`, `security audit --output`, `loop record --output`, and `explain --markdown` resolve against the working directory instead of `--target`. A path flag not listed here is confined only when the command that reads it routes through the boundary. A governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions.
- `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess` and `governance report` reject output destinations that resolve to the target root, including `.`, an absolute root path, `nested/..`, and symlink or junction aliases of the root. Output subdirectories and defaults are unchanged.
- `wiki export` and `handoff bundle` check all planned file destinations and their parent directories before the first write, including copied wiki pages and optional replay files. An existing child symlink or junction outside the target refuses the export without changing output files. `wiki export` also checks every page it copies, so a page that shares its bytes with another name refuses the export before anything is written, including when both names stay inside the target. Concurrent link replacement is not prevented.
- A planned output file that shares its bytes with another name — a hard link, or a link to one — is refused before the write by `wiki export`, `handoff bundle`, `workflow assess --output-dir`, `governance report --output`, `ledger export --out`, `knowledge context-review-sample --output`, `gate --plan` and `accept --plan` (the plan file they edit in place), `handoff` (the `session-handoff.md` it overwrites), `hooks install` (the `pre-commit` hook and its `.amber-backup` it overwrites), `knowledge plan propose` (the plan file it overwrites when `--force`) and `sync --execute` / scaffold refresh (the controlled template files it overwrites and their `.bak` copies) — and `amber context benchmark` applies the same refusal to the benchmark reports it persists — even when both names stay inside the target. A link to a single in-target file is still written through, so it replaces that file's bytes; `workflow assess` is the exception, because it confines its output file to the `--output-dir` and so refuses a link whose referent sits elsewhere in the target. Like the child-link check above, this is checked before the write, so a link swapped in during the write is not caught.
- `handoff validate --bundle-dir .` and `workflow assess --handoff-bundle-dir .` still accept root-level bundles as read-only inputs. Explicit handoff validation paths outside `--target` are refused.
- Writing governance state goes through two shared helpers — the in-place JSON writer and the append-only JSONL ledger append — and both refuse a leaf that shares its bytes with another name. That covers the `.amber/` writers built on them (context pages and Loadouts, audit and event ledgers) without each one repeating the check; a raw write outside those helpers is guarded only where its own surface names it above.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
